subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the 'Conventions' paragraph and basic fact (F3) of the parent proof (η_{a,t} is an affine homeomorphism and measurable embedding with inverse v ↦ a + tv; η_{y,s}∘η_{a,t} = η_{a+ty,ts}; η_{a,t}^{−1}(B_ρ(w)) = B_{tρ}(a + tw); η_{a,t}(B_ρ(v)) = B_{ρ/t}(η_{a,t}(v)); μ^{a,t}(A) = t^{−n}μ(η_{a,t}^{−1}A); (μ^{a,t})^{y,s} = μ^{a+ty,ts}; ℝ^P is a C² submanifold of itself via ψ = id), and parent step 3(h) (restriction commutes with the push-forward by the measurable embedding η). Simon uses these identities tacitly in 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1), (10) (chapter-07.txt line 467).
Notation: for s > 0, η_{a,s}(v) = −(s^{−1}•a) + s^{−1}•v = s^{−1}(v − a) (contract dilation, dilationCLM P s = s^{−1}•id).
0. (η is an affine homeomorphism.) For s > 0, v ↦ a + s·v is a two-sided inverse of η_{a,s}: s^{−1}((a + s v) − a) = v and a + s·s^{−1}(v − a) = v. Both maps are continuous (affine), so η_{a,s} is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero s^{−1} followed by Homeomorph.addLeft (−(s^{−1}•a))); hence it is measurable, a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding), injective, surjective and an open map, and ‖η_{a,s}(v) − η_{a,s}(v')‖ = s^{−1}‖v − v'‖.
1. (ℝ^P is a C² submanifold of itself.) Let y ∈ univ. Take d = P, V := univ ⊆ Euclid P, W := univ ⊆ Euclid P and ψ := id. Then V and W are open, y ∈ W, ψ is C^∞, so ContDiffOn ℝ 2 ψ V (contDiff_id.contDiffOn), ψ is injective on V, ψ '' V = univ = W ∩ univ, for every compact K ⊆ W the set V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) = K is compact, and for every z ∈ V, fderiv ℝ ψ z = ContinuousLinearMap.id (fderiv_id) is injective. Hence IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 P univ.
2. For Borel A: (ofReal(s^{−n})•ν.map η_{a,s})(A) = ofReal(s^{−n})·(ν.map η_{a,s})(A) (Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul) = ofReal(s^{−n})·ν(η_{a,s}^{−1}(A)) (Measure.map_apply, η measurable by 0, A measurable).
3. For v ∈ ℝ^P: v ∈ η_{a,s}^{−1}(B_ρ(w)) ⟺ ‖s^{−1}(v − a) − w‖ < ρ ⟺ s^{−1}‖v − (a + s w)‖ < ρ (since s^{−1}(v − a) − w = s^{−1}(v − (a + s w)) and ‖s^{−1}u‖ = s^{−1}‖u‖) ⟺ ‖v − (a + s w)‖ < sρ (multiply by s > 0) ⟺ v ∈ B_{sρ}(a + s w).
4. If ‖v − c‖ < ρ then ‖η_{a,s}(v) − η_{a,s}(c)‖ = s^{−1}‖v − c‖ < ρ/s, so η_{a,s}(B_ρ(c)) ⊆ B_{ρ/s}(η_{a,s}(c)). Conversely, if ‖u − η_{a,s}(c)‖ < ρ/s, put v := a + s u; then η_{a,s}(v) = u and, as c = a + s·η_{a,s}(c), ‖v − c‖ = s‖u − η_{a,s}(c)‖ < ρ, so u ∈ η_{a,s}(B_ρ(c)).
5. η_{a,s} is surjective (0), so η_{a,s}(univ) = univ; it is a homeomorphism, hence an open map, so η_{a,s}(A) is open for open A (Homeomorph.isOpenMap).
6. For every v: η_{y,t}(η_{a,s}(v)) = t^{−1}(s^{−1}(v − a) − y) = (st)^{−1}(v − a − s y) = η_{a+sy,st}(v), using (st)^{−1} = s^{−1}t^{−1}. So η_{y,t}∘η_{a,s} = η_{a+sy,st} (funext) and η_{y,t}(η_{a,s}(A)) = (η_{y,t}∘η_{a,s})(A) = η_{a+sy,st}(A) (Set.image_image).
7. ofReal(t^{−n})•(ofReal(s^{−n})•ν.map η_{a,s}).map η_{y,t} = ofReal(t^{−n})•ofReal(s^{−n})•(ν.map η_{a,s}).map η_{y,t} (Measure.map_smul) = (ofReal(t^{−n})·ofReal(s^{−n}))•ν.map(η_{y,t}∘η_{a,s}) (smul_smul; Measure.map_map with both maps measurable) = ofReal((st)^{−n})•ν.map η_{a+sy,st}, by step 6 and ofReal(t^{−n})·ofReal(s^{−n}) = ofReal(t^{−n}·s^{−n}) = ofReal((st)^{−n}) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, both factors ≥ 0; mul_inv, mul_pow).
8. η_{0,1}(v) = −(1^{−1}•0) + 1^{−1}•v = v, so η_{0,1} = id. Hence ν.map η_{0,1} = ν (Measure.map_id), ofReal(1^{−n}) = ofReal 1 = 1, 1•ν = ν, and η_{0,1}(A) = A (Set.image_id).

Since η is a measurable embedding (0), (ν.map η).restrict(η(B)) = (ν.restrict(η^{−1}(η(B)))).map η (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map) = (ν.restrict B).map η, because η is injective, so η^{−1}(η(B)) = B (Set.preimage_image_eq). Restriction commutes with scalar multiplication ((c•μ).restrict S = c•(μ.restrict S), Measure.restrict_smul). Source: parent step 4(d) together with basic facts (F1) and (F2)(2),(3); Simon 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1), (8) and (10) (chapter-07.txt lines 454–467: blow-ups at scales tending to 0 minimize in all of ℝ^{n+ℓ}, and η_{x,λ#} preserves the class), and Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 (push-forward by the proper affine map η, ∂η_# = η_#∂).
Notation: η := dilation y t, B := blowUp S y t (ne_of_gt t>0) ∈ 𝒟_n(η(univ)).
1. (Domain.) η(univ) = univ by the sibling ambient_calculus (5).
2. (Minimality.) The sibling blowup_scaling (Submission.dtc_blowUp_scaling) with U := univ (open), A := univ, x := y, λ := t > 0 and 0 < n, part (3): IsMinimizingIn S univ implies IsMinimizingIn B (η(univ)).
3. (Representation and weight.) Part (2) of the same sibling, applied to R (R represents S), gives an IMRep R₁ in η(univ) representing B with R₁.measure(s) = ofReal(t^{−n})·R.measure(η^{−1}(s)) for every Borel s. By ambient_calculus (2), the right side equals (ofReal(t^{−n})•R.measure.map η)(s). Two measures that agree on every measurable set are equal (Measure.ext), so R₁.measure = ofReal(t^{−n})•R.measure.map η.
4. (Boundary, (F1).) Write n = m + 1 (n ≥ 1), so BoundaryVanishes means vanishing of GeometricCurrentOn.boundary. By the contract definition, B = (S.restrictDomain h).affinePushforward L b hp with L = dilationCLM P t = t^{−1}•id, b = −(t^{−1}•y), h : η^{−1}(η(univ)) ⊆ univ and hp the properness of v ↦ b + L v. (a) Boundary commutes with the affine push-forward: (X.affinePushforward L b hp).boundary = X.boundary.affinePushforward L b hp (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward). (b) Boundary commutes with restriction of the domain: for ω ∈ 𝒟^m(W) (W := η^{−1}(η(univ))), ((S.restrictDomain h).boundary)(ω) = (S.restrictDomain h)(dω) = S(ι(dω)) and ((S.boundary).restrictDomain h)(ω) = S.boundary(ι ω) = S(d(ι ω)), where ι is testFormOnInclusion h; ι(dω) and d(ι ω) are test forms on univ with the same underlying differential form (the exterior derivative of the underlying form of ω; testFormOnInclusion_coe, exteriorDerivativeTestOn), hence equal (Subtype.ext), and the two currents agree (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). (c) Since S.boundary = 0, its restriction and its affine push-forward are the zero current (each evaluates the zero functional). Therefore B.boundary = ((S.restrictDomain h).boundary).affinePushforward L b hp = ((S.boundary).restrictDomain h).affinePushforward L b hp = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes B. (Equivalently, part (iv) of dtc_blowUp_algebra, ∂(blowUp T x λ) = blowUp (∂T) x λ, which is in the accepted history of blowup_scaling.)
5. (Transport to the domain univ.) Prove the auxiliary statement: for every set V with V = univ, every B' ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and every IMRep R₂ in V with IsMinimizingIn B' V, BoundaryVanishes B', R₂ represents B' and R₂.measure = ofReal(t^{−n})•R.measure.map η, there are S' ∈ 𝒟_n(univ) and R' ∈ IMRep univ n with the same four properties. Proof: substitute V = univ (subst on the equation hV : V = univ, V a variable) and take S' := B', R' := R₂; substitution changes none of the four properties (the measure of an IMRep does not depend on its domain index). Apply the auxiliary statement with V := η(univ) (step 1), B' := B, R₂ := R₁ and the facts of steps 2–4. This gives S' and R' as claimed. ∎

(DEM) is the frozen statement of Submission.idtp_imrep_measure_density_ae: for all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every U ⊆ ℝ^P and every R ∈ IMRep U n (carrier M, multiplicity θ : ℝ^P → ℕ) whose weight R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ satisfies R.measure(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, for μHE[n]-a.e. x the ratio R.measure(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) (in [0, ∞], ω_n = unitBallVolume n) tends to 1_M(x)·θ(x) as ρ → 0⁺. Then for all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every U ⊆ ℝ^P and every R ∈ IMRep U n with R.measure(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P: R.measure = μHE[n].withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(d(x))), where d(x) := (limsup_{ρ→0⁺} R.measure(B_ρ(x))/(unitBallVolume n·ofReal(ρ^n))).toReal (limsup in [0, ∞] along 𝓝[>]0).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent basic fact (F9) (parent step 2(iii); Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) and Theorem 1.9: for a countably n-rectifiable H^n-measurable M and locally H^n-integrable θ, Θ^n(θH^n⌞M, x) = θ(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M and = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∉ M).
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult (ℕ-valued), μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ.restrict M).withDensity(x ↦ (θ x : [0, ∞])); g(x) := Set.indicator M (y ↦ (θ y : [0, ∞])) x; r(x, ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x))/(unitBallVolume n·ofReal(ρ^n)); L(x) := limsup_{ρ→0⁺} r(x, ρ) ∈ [0, ∞].
1. (DEM) applied to P, n, U, R (n ≥ 1 and μ(K) ≠ ∞ for compact K are our hypotheses) gives: for Hⁿ-a.e. x, r(x, ·) → g(x) along 𝓝[>]0.
2. Fix x at which this convergence holds. The filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ is not the bottom filter (NeBot instance for nhdsWithin of Ioi), so the limsup of a convergent function is its limit (Filter.Tendsto.limsup_eq): L(x) = g(x). Since g(x) is either 0 or the coercion of the natural number θ(x), g(x) ≠ ∞, hence ofReal(L(x).toReal) = L(x) = g(x) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
3. By steps 1–2, (x ↦ ofReal(L(x).toReal)) =ᵐ[Hⁿ] g (Filter.Eventually.mono). Hence Hⁿ.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(L(x).toReal)) = Hⁿ.withDensity g (withDensity_congr_ae; no measurability of the integrand is required).
4. M is measurable (IMRep.measurableSet_carrier), so Hⁿ.withDensity(Set.indicator M (y ↦ θ y)) = (Hⁿ.restrict M).withDensity(y ↦ θ y) (withDensity_indicator), which is μ by the definition of IMRep.measure.
5. Steps 3 and 4 give μ = Hⁿ.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(L(x).toReal)); the integrand is literally fun x => ENNReal.ofReal ((limsup (fun ρ => R.measure (ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0)).toReal). ∎
proof_key_steps: (DEM) gives, for Hⁿ-a.e. x, convergence of the density ratio to the finite value 1_M(x)θ(x).
Where the ratio converges, limsup = limit along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>]0, and ofReal ∘ toReal is the identity on finite values.
withDensity_congr_ae and withDensity_indicator identify Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ d) with (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ = R.measure.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1(c),(d) and step 4(b),(c) ((c1)–(c3)); Simon 7.3.1(1) and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 302–310 and 326–330: the monotonicity formula 4.7 of Ch. 4 gives existence and upper semicontinuity of Θ), and Simon 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1), (2), (4) and (11) (lines 420–470: density bounds for T and for every member of 𝒯).
Conventions. ω_n := unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n; for n ≥ 1 it satisfies 0 < ω_n < ∞ (nonempty open bounded set). For τ > 0, ofReal(τ^n) ∈ (0, ∞). All divisions in [0, ∞] below are by such finite nonzero quantities, so the usual cancellations hold (ENNReal.div_mul_cancel, ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left).
Part (A).
A1. Apply (MON) to P, n, d, U, N, T; its hypotheses are among ours. Part (i) with our compact K ⊆ U gives Λ ≥ 0 such that, whenever closedBall p ρ ⊆ K, f_p(τ) := ofReal(e^{Λτ}/τ^n)·M_{B_τ(p)}(T) is nondecreasing on (0, ρ). Part (iii) gives Θ with HasMassDensity T q (Θ q) for all q ∈ U, and part (iv) gives 1 ≤ θ whenever q ∈ spt T and HasMassDensity T q θ. Fix this Λ; it depends only on K.
A2. Let p, σ, ρ be as in (A). Since 0 < σ < ρ, p ∈ closedBall p ρ ⊆ K ⊆ U. By the sibling im_mass_measure (Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure; U open, R represents T), part (b): p ∈ U and R.measure(B_ε(p)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0 give p ∈ spt T; part (a): M_{B_τ(p)}(T) = R.measure(B_τ(p)) for every τ ∈ (0, ρ) (B_τ(p) is open and ⊆ closedBall p ρ ⊆ U).
A3. (Limit at 0⁺.) HasMassDensity T p Θ(p) means 0 ≤ Θ(p) and q(τ) := M_{B_τ(p)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(τ^n)) → ofReal Θ(p) as τ → 0⁺. For τ > 0, ofReal(e^{Λτ}/τ^n) = ofReal(e^{Λτ})/ofReal(τ^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos), so f_p(τ) = ofReal(e^{Λτ})·ω_n·q(τ). As τ → 0⁺, ofReal(e^{Λτ}) → ofReal(e^0) = 1 (continuity), hence f_p(τ) → ω_n·ofReal Θ(p) (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul and Tendsto.const_mul; all limits are finite).
A4. (Monotone lower bound.) For τ ∈ (0, σ], f_p(τ) ≤ f_p(σ) because f_p is nondecreasing on (0, ρ) and σ < ρ. The set (0, σ] belongs to 𝓝[>]0, so letting τ → 0⁺ (le_of_tendsto) gives ω_n·ofReal Θ(p) ≤ f_p(σ). By A1 (iv) with p ∈ spt T, Θ(p) ≥ 1, so ω_n ≤ ω_n·ofReal Θ(p) ≤ f_p(σ) = ofReal(e^{Λσ}/σ^n)·R.measure(B_σ(p)).
A5. Multiply both sides by ofReal(e^{−Λσ}σ^n) = ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)})·ofReal(σ^n). Since ofReal(e^{−Λσ}σ^n)·ofReal(e^{Λσ}/σ^n) = ofReal(1) = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, Real.exp_neg), we obtain ofReal(e^{−(Λσ)})·(ω_n·ofReal(σ^n)) ≤ R.measure(B_σ(p)). This proves (A).
Part (B). Let S, R be as in (B).
B0. ((MON) for S.) Apply (MON) with P, n, d := P, U = N := ℝ^P and T := S: 1 ≤ n ≤ P ≤ P; ℝ^P is open; IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 P univ by the sibling ambient_calculus (1); (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅; univ ∩ univ = univ, so IsMinimizingIn S (univ ∩ univ) and spt S ⊆ univ ∩ univ; ∂S = 0. It gives: (ii) since N = univ, for every w and every R₀ (B_{R₀}(w) ⊆ univ), τ ↦ ofReal(1/τ^n)·M_{B_τ(w)}(S) is nondecreasing on (0, R₀); (iii) Θ_S with HasMassDensity S w (Θ_S w) for every w; (iv) 1 ≤ θ for w ∈ spt S and HasMassDensity S w θ. By im_mass_measure with U = univ: M_W(S) = R.measure(W) for every open W, and w ∈ spt S ⟺ R.measure(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0.
B1. Let w satisfy R.measure(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0; then w ∈ spt S by B0. Let ρ > 0 and R₀ := ρ + 1. Exactly as in A3–A5 with Λ = 0 (ofReal(1/τ^n) = ofReal(e^{0·τ}/τ^n)): g(τ) := ofReal(1/τ^n)·R.measure(B_τ(w)) is nondecreasing on (0, ρ + 1), tends to ω_n·ofReal Θ_S(w) ≥ ω_n as τ → 0⁺, hence ω_n ≤ g(ρ), i.e. ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) ≤ R.measure(B_ρ(w)).
B2. If some w has R.measure(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0, then by B1, R.measure(ℝ^P) ≥ R.measure(B_ρ(w)) ≥ ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) for every ρ > 0; as ω_n > 0 and ρ^n → ∞ (n ≥ 1), R.measure(ℝ^P) = ∞. Otherwise every w has ε_w > 0 with R.measure(B_{ε_w}(w)) = 0; B_{ε_w}(w) is a neighbourhood of w and ℝ^P is second countable, so R.measure(ℝ^P) = 0 (measure_null_of_locally_null with s = univ). Hence R.measure(univ) = 0 ∨ R.measure(univ) = ∞.
B3 (⇒). Assume HasMassDensity S w θ: 0 ≤ θ and M_{B_ρ(w)}(S)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → ofReal θ as ρ → 0⁺. By B0, M_{B_ρ(w)}(S) = R.measure(B_ρ(w)) for every ρ (balls are open), so the ratio formed with R.measure tends to ofReal θ; along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>]0 its limsup is ofReal θ (Filter.Tendsto.limsup_eq), and (ofReal θ).toReal = θ because θ ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal).
B3 (⇐). Assume θ = (limsup …).toReal. By B0 (iii), HasMassDensity S w (Θ_S w), so by (⇒) Θ_S w = (limsup …).toReal = θ. Hence HasMassDensity S w θ. ∎
proof_key_steps: (MON)(i),(iii),(iv) at p ∈ spt T: the nondecreasing quantity ofReal(e^{Λτ}/τ^n)·M_{B_τ(p)}(T) tends to ω_nΘ(p) ≥ ω_n as τ → 0⁺, so it is ≥ ω_n at every σ < ρ; im_mass_measure turns mass into weight and measure-support into spt T.
For minimizing cycles of ℝ^P, (MON) applies with U = N = ℝ^P (ambient_calculus (1)); part (ii) gives the bound with Λ = 0 at every radius.
The bound ω_nρ^n forces infinite total mass at a support point; with no support point the weight is locally null, hence zero.
HasMassDensity is convergence of the ratio, so θ is the toReal of the limsup; (iii) supplies the converse.

Source: parent step 4(e) and step 5 with basic facts (F4), (F5), (F7), (F8); Simon 7.3.1(2) (existence of tangent cones; statement chapter-07.txt lines 302–310, proof from line 326) and 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1), (8) (chapter-07.txt lines 454–466: limits of blow-ups at scales tending to 0 minimize in all of ℝ^{n+ℓ}).
Notation: P := n + k; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); η_{a,s} := dilation a s; μ := R.measure. 'Vague convergence' of ν_j to ν means ∫ f dν_j → ∫ f dν for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ.
Part (A).
1. (Localization.) G is open and p ∈ G, so fix δ > 0 with B_δ(p) ⊆ G. For s > 0, by the sibling ambient_calculus (9) (with B := G, Borel), (μ⌞G)^{p,s} = (μ^{p,s})⌞η_{p,s}(G), and η_{p,s}(G) ⊇ η_{p,s}(B_δ(p)) = B_{δ/s}(0) (ambient_calculus (4), η_{p,s}(p) = 0). Let f be continuous with compact support; then tsupport f ⊆ closedBall 0 M_f for some M_f ≥ 0. If tsupport f ⊆ B_{δ/s}(0) ⊆ η_{p,s}(G), then ∫ f d(μ⌞G)^{p,s} = ∫_{η_{p,s}(G)} f dμ^{p,s} = ∫ f dμ^{p,s} (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, since f = 0 off tsupport f; η_{p,s}(G) is open, hence measurable). Because δ/λ_j → ∞, tsupport f ⊆ B_{δ/λ_j}(0) for all large j. Notation. B := B_{2r}(z); η_{a,s} := dilation a s; for a measure ν and s > 0, ν^{a,s} := ofReal(s^{−n})•ν.map(η_{a,s}); m := μ(B) ∈ (0, ∞); ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞). 0. (Basic formulas.) (a) For Borel A: μ₀(A) = ofReal(r^{−n})·μ(η_{z,r}^{−1}(A) ∩ B) (AC (2), Measure.restrict_apply). (b) η_{z,r}^{−1}(B_2(0)) = B_{2r}(z) = B (AC (3)), so μ₀(B_2(0)ᶜ) = ofReal(r^{−n})·μ(Bᶜ ∩ B) = 0 and μ₀(ℝ^P) = ofReal(r^{−n})·m ∈ (0, ∞). (c) For λ > 0 and Borel A: μ₀^{x,λ}(A) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·μ₀(η_{x,λ}^{−1}(A)) (AC (2)); in particular μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·ofReal(r^{−n})·m, and μ₀^{x,λ}(G_{x,λ}ᶜ) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·μ₀(B_2(0)ᶜ) = 0 (η_{x,λ} is bijective, so η_{x,λ}^{−1}(G_{x,λ}ᶜ) = B_2(0)ᶜ). (d) For w ∈ ℝ^P and σ > 0: μ₀^{x,λ}(B_σ(w)) = ofReal((rλ)^{−n})·μ(B_{rλσ}(z + r(x + λw)) ∩ B), by (c), (a) and AC (3) twice (η_{x,λ}^{−1}(B_σ(w)) = B_{λσ}(x + λw) and η_{z,r}^{−1}(B_{λσ}(x + λw)) = B_{rλσ}(z + r(x + λw))) and ofReal(λ^{−n})·ofReal(r^{−n}) = ofReal((rλ)^{−n}). (e) The affine bijection v ↦ z + r(x + λv) maps G_{x,λ} onto B (v ∈ G_{x,λ} ⟺ x + λv ∈ B_2(0) ⟺ z + r(x + λv) ∈ B) and closedBall w σ onto closedBall (z + r(x + λw)) (rλσ). Hence closedBall w σ ⊆ G_{x,λ} implies closedBall (z + r(x + λw)) (rλσ) ⊆ B, and then the intersection with B in (d) can be dropped: μ₀^{x,λ}(B_σ(w)) = ofReal((rλ)^{−n})·μ(B_{rλσ}(z + r(x + λw))).
1. (Support relation; parent step 7.) Let w ∈ B_2(0) and δ := (2 − ‖w‖)/2 > 0, so closedBall w δ ⊆ B_2(0) = G_{0,1} (AC (8): η_{0,1} = id and μ₀^{0,1} = μ₀). For 0 < ε ≤ δ, 0(e) with x = 0, λ = 1 gives μ₀(B_ε(w)) = ofReal(r^{−n})·μ(B_{rε}(z + rw)). (⇒) Given ε' > 0, let ε := min(δ, ε'/r) > 0: then ofReal(r^{−n})·μ(B_{rε}(z + rw)) = μ₀(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0, so μ(B_{rε}(z + rw)) ≠ 0, and B_{rε}(z + rw) ⊆ B_{ε'}(z + rw) gives μ(B_{ε'}(z + rw)) ≠ 0. (⇐) Given ε > 0, let ε₁ := min(ε, δ): μ₀(B_{ε₁}(w)) = ofReal(r^{−n})·μ(B_{rε₁}(z + rw)) ≠ 0 (both factors nonzero), and μ₀(B_ε(w)) ≥ μ₀(B_{ε₁}(w)) > 0.
2. (Injectivity; parent step 3(b),(c).) Suppose λ, λ' > 0 and μ₀^{x,λ} = μ₀^{x',λ'}. Total masses (0(c)): ofReal(λ^{−n})·c = ofReal(λ'^{−n})·c with c := ofReal(r^{−n})·m ∈ (0, ∞), so λ^{−n} = λ'^{−n}; since n ≥ 1 and λ, λ' > 0, λ^{−1} = λ'^{−1} (pow_left_injective on [0, ∞)) and λ = λ'. Barycenters: by 0(b), μ₀ is a finite measure and ‖v‖ < 2 for μ₀-a.e. v, so v ↦ v is μ₀-integrable; put b₀ := ∫ v dμ₀(v) and m₀ := μ₀(ℝ^P).toReal > 0. By integral_smul_measure and integral_map (η_{x,λ} measurable, id continuous), ∫ v dμ₀^{x,λ}(v) = λ^{−n}·∫ η_{x,λ}(v) dμ₀(v) = λ^{−n}·(λ^{−1}b₀ − λ^{−1}m₀x), using η_{x,λ}(v) = λ^{−1}v − λ^{−1}x, linearity of the integral (integral_add, integral_smul) and ∫ const dμ₀ = m₀·const (integral_const). Equal measures have equal integrals, so (with λ = λ') λ^{−n−1}(b₀ − m₀x) = λ^{−n−1}(b₀ − m₀x'), hence m₀x = m₀x' and x = x'.
3. (Mass.) By 0(c), μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·ofReal(r^{−n})·m, a product of factors in (0, ∞); so it is ≠ 0 and ≠ ∞.
4. (Domains; parent step 3(d).) By AC (4), G_{x,λ} = η_{x,λ}(B_2(0)) = B_{2/λ}(−λ^{−1}x) (η_{x,λ}(0) = −λ^{−1}x), which is open. For ‖v‖ < 2: ‖v + λ^{−1}x‖ ≤ ‖v‖ + λ^{−1}‖x‖ < 2 + λ^{−1}(1 − λ) = 1 + λ^{−1} ≤ 2λ^{−1} (since λ ≤ 1), so B_2(0) ⊆ G_{x,λ}. Likewise for ‖v‖ < λ^{−1}: ‖v + λ^{−1}x‖ < λ^{−1} + λ^{−1}(1 − λ) < 2λ^{−1}, so B_{1/λ}(0) ⊆ G_{x,λ} (used in 5c).
5. (Domain recovery under vague limits; parent step 12.)
 5a. (Continuity in the parameters; parent step 3(g).) Let f be continuous with compact support and F(x, λ) := ∫ f dμ₀^{x,λ}. By integral_smul_measure and integral_map, F(x, λ) = λ^{−n}·∫ f(η_{x,λ}(v)) dμ₀(v). For each v, (x, λ) ↦ f(λ^{−1}(v − x)) is continuous on ℝ^P × (0, ∞); |f(·)| ≤ sup|f| < ∞, a constant that is μ₀-integrable (μ₀ finite). By dominated convergence (continuousOn version of continuous_of_dominated, or tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence along sequences) and continuity of λ ↦ λ^{−n} on (0, ∞), F is continuous on ℝ^P × (0, ∞).
 5b. (Uniqueness of vague limits, parent (F6).) If ν₁, ν₂ are measures on ℝ^P, finite on compact sets, with ∫ f dν₁ = ∫ f dν₂ for all continuous compactly supported f, then ν₁ = ν₂. Proof: for open O and integers m ≥ 1 let f_m(v) := min(1, m·infDist(v, Oᶜ))·min(1, (m − ‖v‖)⁺) (first factor := 1 if O = ℝ^P). Each f_m is continuous with support in closedBall 0 m, 0 ≤ f_m ≤ 1_O, and f_m ↑ 1_O pointwise (for v ∈ O, infDist(v, Oᶜ) > 0 since Oᶜ is closed). By monotone convergence ν_i(O) = lim_m ∫ f_m dν_i, so ν₁(O) = ν₂(O). Open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra (isPiSystem_isOpen, borel = generateFrom of open sets), and the open balls B_m(0) have finite measure and cover ℝ^P, so ν₁ = ν₂ (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion). (Equivalently: finite on compacts gives IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts, hence local finiteness and regularity on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P (Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure), and Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported applies.)
 5c. (Proof of (5).) K is compact, so K ⊆ closedBall 0 R_K for some R_K ≥ 1. If λ_i < 1/R_K for some i, then K ⊆ closedBall 0 R_K ⊆ B_{1/λ_i}(0) ⊆ G_{x_i,λ_i} (step 4), contradicting K ⊄ G_{x_i,λ_i}. So λ_i ≥ λ₀ := 1/R_K > 0 for every i. The set Π := {(x, λ) : λ₀ ≤ λ ≤ 1, ‖x‖ ≤ 1 − λ} ⊆ ℝ^P × ℝ is closed and bounded, hence compact, and contains every (x_i, λ_i). By sequential compactness (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are a strictly increasing ψ and (x*, λ*) ∈ Π with (x_{ψ(i)}, λ_{ψ(i)}) → (x*, λ*); (x*, λ*) is admissible since λ* ≥ λ₀ > 0. For every continuous compactly supported f: by 5a, ∫ f dμ₀^{x_{ψ(i)},λ_{ψ(i)}} → ∫ f dμ₀^{x*,λ*}; by hypothesis (composed with ψ, StrictMono.tendsto_atTop) the same integrals converge to ∫ f dν; by uniqueness of limits in ℝ, ∫ f dν = ∫ f dμ₀^{x*,λ*}. ν is finite on compacts by hypothesis and μ₀^{x*,λ*} is finite (step 3), so 5b gives ν = μ₀^{x*,λ*}. Finally suppose K ⊆ G_{x*,λ*} = B_{2/λ*}(c*), c* := −x*/λ*. K ≠ ∅ (otherwise K ⊆ G_{x_{ψ(0)},λ_{ψ(0)}} trivially), so the continuous function v ↦ ‖v − c*‖ attains a maximum M < 2/λ* on K. Put γ := (2/λ* − M)/2 > 0. Since c_i := −x_{ψ(i)}/λ_{ψ(i)} → c* and 2/λ_{ψ(i)} → 2/λ* (continuity on λ > 0), for large i we have ‖c_i − c*‖ < γ and 2/λ_{ψ(i)} > 2/λ* − γ; then every v ∈ K satisfies ‖v − c_i‖ ≤ M + ‖c* − c_i‖ < M + γ = 2/λ* − γ < 2/λ_{ψ(i)}, i.e. K ⊆ G_{x_{ψ(i)},λ_{ψ(i)}}, a contradiction. Hence K ⊄ G_{x*,λ*}, and (x, λ) := (x*, λ*) satisfies (5).
6. (Non-homogeneity; parent step 14.) Let f be as in (6) and ν := μHE[n].withDensity f. For t > 0, the sibling withdensity_dilate (Submission.dimred_cs_mi_withDensity_dilate with λ := t, its hypothesis f(t·w) = f(w) holding for all w, and the Borel set B_1(0)) gives ν((v ↦ t v) '' B_1(0)) = ofReal(t^n)·ν(B_1(0)), and (v ↦ t v) '' B_1(0) = B_t(0) (smul_ball, ‖t‖ = t). If ν(B_1(0)) = 0, then ν(B_t(0)) = 0 for all t > 0 and ν(ℝ^P) = ν(⋃_{m≥1} B_m(0)) = 0 (measure_iUnion_null). If ν(B_1(0)) ≠ 0, then ν(ℝ^P) ≥ ν(B_t(0)) = ofReal(t^n)·ν(B_1(0)) for all t > 0, and ofReal(t^n) → ∞ as t → ∞ (n ≥ 1), so ν(ℝ^P) = ∞. In both cases ν(ℝ^P) ∈ {0, ∞}, while μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) ∉ {0, ∞} by step 3. Hence μ₀^{x,λ} ≠ ν.
7. (Transferred lower bound; parent step 13.) Let Λ₀, x, y, λ, ρ be as in (7); put s := rλ ∈ (0, r] and p := z + r(x + λy). By 0(e) applied to closedBall y σ ⊆ closedBall y ρ ⊆ G_{x,λ}: closedBall p (sρ) ⊆ B, and μ₀^{x,λ}(B_σ(y)) = ofReal(s^{−n})·μ(B_{sσ}(p)) for every 0 < σ ≤ ρ.
 7a. μ(B_{ε'}(p)) ≠ 0 for every ε' > 0: with σ := min(ρ, ε'/s) > 0, ofReal(s^{−n})·μ(B_{sσ}(p)) = μ₀^{x,λ}(B_σ(y)) ≠ 0 by hypothesis, so μ(B_{sσ}(p)) ≠ 0, and B_{sσ}(p) ⊆ B_{ε'}(p).
 7b. closedBall p (sρ) is compact and contained in the open set B, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ (closedBall p (sρ)) ⊆ B (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open), and closedBall p (sρ + δ) ⊆ cthickening δ (closedBall p (sρ)) (a point q with ‖q − p‖ ≤ sρ + δ is within δ of p + min(1, sρ/‖q − p‖)(q − p) ∈ closedBall p (sρ)). Hence closedBall p (sρ + δ) ⊆ B ⊆ closedBall z (2r).
 7c. The hypothesis on μ, applied to p (by 7a), σ := sρ and ρ' := sρ + δ (0 < sρ < sρ + δ, closedBall p ρ' ⊆ closedBall z (2r) by 7b), gives ofReal(e^{−(Λ₀sρ)})·(ω_n·ofReal((sρ)^n)) ≤ μ(B_{sρ}(p)).
 7d. Therefore μ₀^{x,λ}(B_ρ(y)) = ofReal(s^{−n})·μ(B_{sρ}(p)) ≥ ofReal(s^{−n})·ofReal(e^{−(Λ₀sρ)})·ω_n·ofReal(s^n)·ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(e^{−(Λ₀rλρ)})·(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) (ofReal(s^{−n})·ofReal(s^n) = ofReal(1) = 1, (sρ)^n = s^nρ^n). subproblems.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its representing measure, and its support is the support of that measure (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be open, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), where H^n = μHE[n]). Write μ_R := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M. Then: (a) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ U, where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum (in [0, ∞]) of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (b) for every x ∈ U: x ∈ spt T if and only if μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0; (c) every other representation R' of T has the same measure: R'.measure = R.measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ (∀ x ∈ U, (x ∈ T.support ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → R.measure (ball x ε) ≠ 0)) ∧ ∀ R' : IMRep U n, R'.Represents T → R'.measure = R.measure

Use under the selected node: used in the sibling monotonicity_bounds (M_W(T) = μ_R(W) on open W ⊆ U and x ∈ spt T ⟺ μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 ∀ ε, parent (IM-a),(IM-b)), in the sibling tangent_measures (a null ball off spt T, parent (F4)), and in the selected node's own assembly (the support relation of parent step 7 and the passage from measure support to spt S in (M8), parent step 15). The numbered proof below is that node's independently reviewed parent-supplied proof, reproduced unchanged; its 'parent'/'sibling' references are to that node's own parent and siblings.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.8 and Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 224–300 and 733–775), which state these facts as evident; this is the identity "μ_S = R.measure for every representation R, M_W(S) = μ_S(W), spt S = spt μ_S" used throughout the parent proof (its Notation paragraph). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α on ℝ^P, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing multi-indices I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) (for n = 0, |α| = |α()|); dx^I is the dual basis covector.
1. (Pointwise duality.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let α be an n-covector. By multilinearity and alternation, α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where τ^I is the n × n matrix (⟨e_{i_a}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = det(I_n) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, with equality for α_τ := Σ_I det(τ^I) dx^I, which satisfies |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1. (For n = 0 both sides equal |α()| and α_τ := 1.)
2. (Consequences for R.) By the field `orients` of IMRep, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ(x) and a sign σ(x) ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(τ(x)) for every n-covector α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Hence, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. Moreover β(x) := Σ_I ξ(x)(dx^I)·dx^I equals σ(x)·α_{τ(x)} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, so |β(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 there. The coefficients ξ(·)(dx^I) of β are H^n⌞M-measurable because ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient); as μ_R ≪ H^n⌞M, β is μ_R-measurable.
3. (Radon property.) μ_R is a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U) and μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (field locallyIntegrable_mult). Since U is an open subset of ℝ^P, hence σ-compact, locally compact and second countable, the restriction of μ_R to U is a locally finite Borel measure on U and therefore outer regular by open sets and inner regular by compact sets on Borel subsets of U.
4. (Upper bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open and let ω be admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere). By R.Represents T and step 2, T(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫_M θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n = μ_R(W), because ω vanishes off W. Taking ofReal and the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open, K ⊆ W compact and ε > 0. By step 3 choose an open V with K ⊆ V, closure V compact and contained in W, and μ_R(V ∖ K) < ε. By Lusin's theorem (for the finite Radon measure μ_R⌞V and the μ_R-measurable map β of step 2, with values in the finite-dimensional space Λ^n of n-covectors) choose a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < ε and β|_{K'} continuous. Extend β|_{K'} to a continuous map ℝ^P → Λ^n (Tietze, coordinatewise) and compose with the retraction r(α) := α / max(1, |α|) (continuous, |r(α)| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball) to obtain a continuous β̃ with |β̃| ≤ 1 and β̃ = β on K'. Take χ ∈ C_c(V; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on K, and put γ := χ·β̃ (continuous, |γ| ≤ 1, compact support in V). Let γ_j := γ * ϱ_{1/j} be the coordinatewise convolution with a standard mollifier. For all large j, γ_j is C^∞, tsupport γ_j is a compact subset of V ⊆ W ⊆ U, |γ_j| ≤ 1 everywhere (Jensen's inequality for the convex function |·|), and γ_j → γ uniformly. So γ_j is admissible for M_W(T) and M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(γ_j). By dominated convergence (dominating function θ·1_{closure V}, integrable by step 3), T(γ_j) = ∫_M θ·ξ(γ_j) dH^n → ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n. On K', ξ(γ) = ξ(β) = 1 μ_R-a.e.; on V ∖ K', |ξ(γ)| ≤ 1; off V, γ = 0. Hence ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(V ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − ε) − 2ε, since μ_R(V ∖ K') ≤ μ_R(V ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K') < 2ε. Therefore M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3ε for every compact K ⊆ W and every ε > 0, and inner regularity of μ_R on the open set W (step 3) gives M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
6. ((b), "if".) Let x ∈ U with μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0, and suppose x ∉ spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T). Then x ∈ W for some open W with closure W compact and contained in U on which T vanishes, i.e. T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Every admissible value in the definition of M_W(T) is ofReal 0 = 0 (and the zero form is admissible), so M_W(T) = 0, and by (a) μ_R(W) = 0. For ε > 0 so small that B_ε(x) ⊆ W we get μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ spt T.
7. ((b), "only if".) Let x ∈ spt T and suppose μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0 for some ε > 0. Choose ε' ∈ (0, ε) with closedBall x ε' ⊆ U (U is open). W := B_{ε'}(x) is open, its closure closedBall x ε' is compact and contained in U, and for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, step 2 gives |T(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ (sup_x |ω(x)|)·μ_R(W) = 0. So T vanishes on W, W belongs to the family defining zeroRegion(T), x ∈ zeroRegion(T), i.e. x ∉ spt T: a contradiction. Hence μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0.
8. ((c).) Let R' be another representation of T. By (a) applied to R and to R', R'.measure(W) = M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ U. Both measures vanish on ℝ^P ∖ U (both carriers lie in U) and are finite on every open W whose closure is a compact subset of U (step 3). The open subsets of U with compact closure in U form a π-system (closed under finite intersections) generating the Borel σ-algebra of U (every open subset of U is a countable union of them), and U is the union of an increasing sequence of them on which both measures are finite. By the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on such a generating π-system, R'.measure(A ∩ U) = R.measure(A ∩ U) for every Borel A, hence R'.measure = R.measure.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet duality: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for the unit simple orientation ξ(x), with equality for the dual covector β(x).
Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) directly from the representation.
Lower bound by Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction to the unit ball, mollification and inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_R.
Support: T vanishes on W ⇔ M_W(T) = 0 ⇔ μ_R(W) = 0, giving spt T = spt μ_R inside U.
Representation independence: two representations agree on open subsets of U, hence (π-system uniqueness, σ-finiteness on U) everywhere.

Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dtc_blowUp_scaling of DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.blowup_scaling-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit a94d596c81cfb78de36a706eb0e81f430f835418, isolated comparator passed). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node; registering it here overlays its accepted candidate history (including its own accepted dependency closure) for the siblings that list it in depends_on and for the selected node. Use under the selected node: used in the sibling cycle_rescale (parent step 4(d): blow-ups of minimizing cycles are minimizing, with weight (μ_S)^{y,t}), in the sibling tangent_measures (parent steps 4(e), 5: the IMReps of the blow-ups have weights μ^{p,λ}), and in the selected node's own assembly (parent step 3(h): an IMRep of η_{z+rx,rλ#}T with weight μ_T^{z+rx,rλ}, for (M2)). The numbered proof below is that node's independently reviewed parent-supplied proof, reproduced unchanged; its 'parent'/'sibling' references are to that node's own parent and siblings.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 (push-forward, chapter-06.txt lines 405–440) and 3.3–3.9 (push-forward of integer multiplicity currents, lines 770–862); the scaling identity (1) in the proof of Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 329–331); invariance of minimality under dilations is used in the proof of 7.3.1 (line 333) and in step 4(iv) of the parent proof ("dilations preserve minimality").
0. Facts about η. η is an affine bijection of ℝ^P with inverse η⁻¹(z) = x + λz and |η(y) − η(y')| = λ⁻¹|y − y'|.
 (i) Hⁿ(η(E)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n] is translation invariant and Hⁿ(cE) = cⁿHⁿ(E) for c > 0: Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Hence for Borel E and Borel g ≥ 0 (or g integrable on η(E)): ∫_{η(E)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_E g∘η dHⁿ.
 (ii) The pullback is (η^#ω)(y)(v₁,…,vₙ) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y))(v₁,…,vₙ); so η^#ω = λ^{−n}(ω∘η), |η^#ω(y)| = λ^{−n}|ω(η(y))| for the Euclidean coefficient norm, and tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω). By the definition of blowUp (affine push-forward of the restriction of T, with η⁻¹(η(U)) = U), S(ω) = T(η^#ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). Conversely every ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) equals η^#ω for exactly one ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), namely ω = λⁿ(ω'∘η⁻¹). The same statements hold for any current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and its push-forward η_#Y(ω) := Y(η^#ω).
 (iii) If ζ(α) = ±α(τ) then ζ(λ^{−n}α) = λ^{−n}ζ(α) (linearity).
1. Mass scaling. Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and W ⊆ ℝ^P. The map ω ↦ ω∘η = λⁿη^#ω is a bijection from the admissible forms for η_#Y on η(W) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), tsupport ω ⊆ η(W), |ω| ≤ 1) onto the admissible forms for Y on W (tsupport(ω∘η) = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(W)) = W and |ω(η(y))| ≤ 1), and η_#Y(ω) = Y(η^#ω) = λ^{−n}Y(ω∘η). Since ofReal(λ^{−n}t) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·ofReal(t) and multiplication by the finite constant ofReal(λ^{−n}) commutes with suprema in [0, ∞], M_{η(W)}(η_#Y) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·M_W(Y). With Y = T this is (1).
2. Representation. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent T and define R' := (M', θ', ξ') with M' := η(M), θ' := θ∘η⁻¹, ξ' := ξ∘η⁻¹.
 - M' is Borel (image of a Borel set under a homeomorphism of ℝ^P) and M' ⊆ η(U).
 - M' is countably n-rectifiable: if M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, then M' ⊆ η(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j (η∘F_j)(ℝⁿ), Hⁿ(η(M₀)) = 0 by 0(i), and each η∘F_j is Lipschitz.
 - θ' is measurable, ℕ-valued, and θ' ≥ 1 on M'.
 - For compact K ⊆ η(U), η⁻¹(K) is a compact subset of U and ∫_{M'∩K} θ' dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_{M∩η⁻¹(K)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by 0(i).
 - ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M' (composition with the homeomorphism η⁻¹, which carries Hⁿ⌞M'-null sets to Hⁿ⌞M-null sets by 0(i)).
 - Orientation: let y ∈ M be such that Q := T_yM exists and ξ(y) orients Q (Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M), and z := η(y). For r > 0 and w ∈ ℝ^P, η_{z,r}(η(w)) = (η(w) − η(y))/r = (w − y)/(λr) = η_{y,λr}(w), so η_{z,r}(M') = η_{y,λr}(M) and ∫_{η_{z,r}(M')} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{y,λr}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q, and ξ'(z) = ξ(y) orients Q. The exceptional set in M' is the η-image of an Hⁿ-null set, hence null.
 - Representation: for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), by 0(ii),(iii) and 0(i): S(ω) = T(η^#ω) = ∫_M θ(y)ξ(y)(λ^{−n}ω(η(y))) dHⁿ(y) = λ^{−n}∫_M (θ'·ξ'(ω))(η(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M'} θ'(z)ξ'(z)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z).
 - Measure: for Borel B, μ_{R'}(B) = ∫_{M'∩B} θ' dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_{M∩η⁻¹(B)} θ dHⁿ = ofReal(λ^{−n})·μ_R(η⁻¹(B)). This proves (2).
3. Minimality. Assume T is minimizing in A. By (2), S is integer multiplicity. Let W' be open with closure W' compact and ⊆ η(U), S' ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)) integer multiplicity with ∂S' = ∂S (n ≥ 1), and spt(S' − S) a compact subset of η(A) ∩ W'.
 (a) Define S'' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) by S''(ω') := S'(λⁿ(ω'∘η⁻¹)), the push-forward of S' by the affine map η⁻¹. It is linear, and continuous because ω' ↦ λⁿ(ω'∘η⁻¹) maps convergent sequences in 𝒟ⁿ(U) to convergent sequences in 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) (supports are mapped by the homeomorphism η, derivatives transform by the chain rule for the affine map). By 0(ii), S''(η^#ω) = S'(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), i.e. η_#S'' = S' (= blowUp S'' x λ); likewise T(ω') = S(λⁿ(ω'∘η⁻¹)), so S'' − T is the η⁻¹-push-forward of S' − S.
 (b) S'' is integer multiplicity: apply the construction of step 2 to S' and the similarity η⁻¹ (which is the dilation η_{−λ⁻¹x, λ⁻¹}; step 2 used only that η is a similarity with ratio λ⁻¹, so it applies verbatim with λ replaced by λ⁻¹ and x by −λ⁻¹x).
 (c) Boundary: exterior differentiation commutes with affine pullback (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm), so ∂S'' is the η⁻¹-push-forward of ∂S' = ∂S, which is the η⁻¹-push-forward of η_#∂T (SimonGMT boundary_affinePushforward); since the two push-forwards are mutually inverse, ∂S'' = ∂T.
